rules.title: Cambridge City Council policy order to ban algorithmic rent-pricing services
rules.requirement: The City Council passed a policy order directing the city manager to draft policy options or ordinance language that would ban residential property management companies from contracting with companies that use algorithmic or AI-driven models to recommend rents. No ordinance has been enacted yet.
rules.key_value: Proposed ban on use of algorithmic/AI rent-recommendation services (policy order only; no ordinance text yet)
rules.coverage_conditions: Unknown; the article describes the target as residential property management companies and large residential property owners. Final coverage depends on ordinance language not yet drafted.
rules.interaction: Parallel Massachusetts state bills (H.1564, S.2983) would also ban the practice.
rules.citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (algorithmic rent pricing), June 2026
rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent.

rules.title: Massachusetts House bill H.1564 banning algorithmic rent-setting
rules.requirement: A House bill that would ban algorithmic rent-pricing practices in the rental market. The bill was pending as of the article date.
rules.key_value: Proposed statewide ban on algorithmic rent-setting
rules.quoted_span: Bills banning the practice in the rental market are also working their way through the Massachusetts state
rules.conflict_note: Status is taken from a June 2026 news article. The 194th General Court's formal sessions may have ended before the query date, so the bill may have died; verify its current status.
